questions.title: Electron transfer in sodium oxide
questions.stimulus: Sodium reacts with oxygen to form the ionic compound sodium oxide. The dot-and-cross diagram shows the ions formed (outer electron shells only).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe, in terms of electrons, how sodium atoms and oxygen atoms form the ions shown.

points.text: Each sodium atom loses 1 (outer) electron to form an Na⁺ ion
Each oxygen atom gains 2 electrons to form an O²⁻ ion
Two sodium atoms transfer 1 electron each to one oxygen atom (giving full outer shells)

accept: electrons are transferred from sodium to oxygen

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the chemical formula of sodium oxide.

parts.label: c
parts.text: State the type of force that holds the Na⁺ and O²⁻ ions together in sodium oxide.

points.text: Strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions

questions.title: Ionic formulae and compound ions
questions.stimulus: The diagram shows how calcium atoms and fluorine atoms react to form calcium fluoride (outer electron shells only).

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the charges on the calcium ion and the fluoride ion, and explain why the formula of calcium fluoride is CaF₂.

points.text: Calcium forms Ca²⁺ (loses 2 electrons) and fluorine forms F⁻ (gains 1 electron)
Two F⁻ ions are needed to balance the 2+ charge of one Ca²⁺ ion (making the compound electrically neutral)

accept: total positive charge equals total negative charge (2+ and 2 × 1−)

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the chemical formulae for (i) magnesium hydroxide and (ii) ammonium sulfate.

points.text: (ii) (NH₄)₂SO₄ (two NH₄⁺ ions with one SO₄²⁻ ion)

questions.title: Properties of giant ionic lattices
questions.stimulus: A chemist tests two white solids, Substance P and Substance Q, and records their melting points and electrical conductivity in the table below.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Substance P has a giant ionic lattice. Explain why Substance P has a very high melting point.

points.text: Giant 3D ionic lattice of oppositely charged ions
Many strong electrostatic forces of attraction acting in all directions
A large amount of (thermal) energy is needed to overcome / break these attractions

accept: strong ionic bonds throughout the lattice

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why Substance P conducts electricity when molten or dissolved in water, but does not conduct when solid.

points.text: When solid, the ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice and cannot move
When molten or in aqueous solution, the ions are free to move and carry electrical charge

reject: delocalised electrons / free electrons carry charge
